title: Example 22-3: Bibliography with Three-Hyphen Dash

illustrates.quote: If two or more works by the same author are listed, a long print dash frequently is substituted for the author’s name. Use the long dash, spaced as shown in print, to reflect this type of print dash accurately. Follow print if other symbols are used.

blocks.text: Puzo, Mario. The Family: A Novel. Completed by Carol Gino. New York: Harper, 2001.
blocks.features: Hanging indent. 'The Family: A Novel.' in italics, including the full stop (the braille passage terminator follows the period).

blocks.text: Rowling, J. K. Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets. New York: Scholastic, 1999.
blocks.features: Hanging indent. 'Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets.' in italics, including the full stop.
emphasis: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets.

blocks.text: ---. Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban. Thorndike, ME: Thorndike, 2000.
blocks.features: Hanging indent. Begins with three bold hyphens in place of the author's name. 'Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban.' in italics, including the full stop.
emphasis: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban.
